Live to Fight: Journey
Live to Fight: People
Live to Fight: Each Scene (3.0)
Live to Fight: Containment Soldier (beta)
Live to Fight: The World (3.0)
Malicious: the arsonist
Patches the character up, leaves the door unlocked, and sets the house on fire less than a minute after waking. If the game does not allow the fire, only the smell of petrol is mentioned.
Board up the windows
Every window of the house is barricaded with planks. The kid only manages one plank per window.
Bigger text for what your character says
For high resolutions such as 4K: the lines your character says about the mod's events are shown in a larger font above them, instead of the game's small speech text.
Leave bodies
Zombies right next to the character when it happens are turned into corpses, and one or two bodies lie in the yard of the house.
The rescue broadcast
With a radio or walkie-talkie switched on, you may hear a message about an evacuation point. Go and see.
Fatal car crashes are caught

A crash that would kill the driver outright starts the rescue instead, as long as a rescue is possible at all. The journal and the character both know it was a crash. When off, only a crash that leaves the character alive but below the dying line is caught.
People in the area
How many rescuers can exist in one save at a time. Once this many know the character it is always one of them who turns up, until one dies or leaves.
Chance lost per rescue (percent)
Each rescue lowers the chance of the next one by this much. With 60 and 25 the fourth near-death is always fatal, with 100 and 25 the fifth.
Chapter II switch on the right-click menu
Off by default: once Chapter II is on, the right-click menu no longer shows its switch. While it is off you still see it, so you can turn it on. Turn this on to always keep the switch on the menu.
Ask about Chapter II when a save starts
The one-time question about Chapter II a few seconds into a save that does not have it yet. Turn this off and you are never asked; Chapter II then stays as set above.
Zombie-free distance (tiles)
Zombies within this many tiles of the house are removed when the character is brought in and again just before they wake.
Remove zombies around the house
Zombies in and around the house are removed before the character wakes up.
Complication chance (percent)
Chance of waking with one extra problem: an infected wound under dirty rags, or otherwise a cold.
Veterans start as containment soldiers
If the new occupation does not appear in your version of the game, turn this on and pick Veteran instead.
Zombies on the last day
How many zombies wait at the end.
The last day
Leave this on. What happens is for you to find out. In worlds without a containment soldier, the outpost has fallen by day 7 and is empty.
Orders needed each day
How many of the day's three orders must be done before you sleep.
Relieved of duty
Go to sleep without enough orders done and you wake up somewhere else, without your post. When off, a missed day is only a warning.
Minutes to get back to the outpost

When the day's orders are done, command orders the officer back to the outpost. Stay more than 50 tiles away for this many real minutes of play and the screen goes black and you head back, in your car if you are in one. 0 switches it off.
Sample chance per kill (percent)
Chance that a zombie you kill on duty gives a sample.
Containment soldier (beta)
Adds the containment soldier occupation: a black screen, then seven days of orders from an outpost at the edge of West Point. Beta: if it is well received, more occupations get their own story.
Uniform in the gear crate
The officer starts in their own clothes. A uniform waits in the gear crate at the outpost with the rest of the kit.
Days before it can happen again
A near-death within this many days of the last rescue is a real death.
The dead rescuer gets up
A few hours after waking, the body of a rescuer who died next to the character turns into a zombie.
A wreck at the crash
Try to place a damaged car next to the character after a crash. If the game refuses, only the debris is placed.
The nurse can cut out a bite

Master switch for the cure. When on, the nurse sometimes turns a bite into a deep wound and removes the infection (the chance is on the People page). When off nobody can. A bitten or infected character is rescued either way and stays bitten.
Deaf while being moved

Gives the character the Deaf trait until they are in the house, so nothing real can be heard. The staged sounds are then played through the interface channel, which may or may not get past the trait. Leave this off unless the staged sounds still play for you with it on.
Days to pay
How long the character has to bring what is asked.
Angry rescuers ask to be paid

A rescuer who has had enough takes more of your things and writes down a price in food and a weapon. Leave it on the floor where the character woke up before the deadline. If it is not paid and the same person finds the character again, they take everything.
Debug mode
Adds right-click entries to trigger a rescue, hurt the character, list houses, show the status and reset the counters. Prints details to the console.
Malicious: the decoy

Leaves the character in the open, half the usual distance away, and makes noise for an hour and a half to draw zombies there while their own group gets away. Fewer zombies are removed around the spot.
Dirty bandages
Wounds are wrapped in dirty rags that need replacing. The nurse always uses clean ones. When off, everyone uses clean ripped sheets.
Rescue when dragged down
Also start the rescue the moment zombies drag the character to the ground.
Shots when dragged down

When the rescue starts because zombies dragged the character down, the black screen opens with eight gunshots coming closer and bodies falling, and the journal mentions the shooting. No noise is made in the world and no zombies are attracted.
A rescuer you know can be dying
Rarely, someone who has found the character at least twice turns up already bitten. They give everything they have, the character wakes up next to their body, and they are gone from the save.
Empty the house
Every container and all loose items in the house are removed. Whoever brought the character there took it as payment.
Near-death rescue
When the character is about to die, they black out and wake up somewhere else, patched up badly and missing things.
How often events happen (percent)
Scales the chance of every event. 100 is the default.
Events around you
Things that happen near you: someone running past, knocking at night, a flare, an engine in the distance.
Malicious: the experimenter
Gives the character something untested. One of five effects: a fever, a crash in energy, shaking and panic, two days of sounds that are not there, or now and then a small benefit.
The first rescue is a kind one
The first rescue of a character is never by a malicious stranger and never ends in a crash, a dead rescuer or a death.
Basement or upper floor: lower still (percent)
Taken off as well when the character goes down below ground or above the ground floor. Added to the indoor loss, so a basement or a bedroom upstairs loses both.
The rescuer can die

The rescuer can be worn down or bitten on the way and die, either beside the character in the house or on the road. Half the wounds are wrapped, there are no painkillers, their kit lies with the body, the journal stops in the middle of a sentence, and that person is gone from the save.
The car can crash

On long journeys the car can go off the road. The character wakes by the roadside part of the way there, not in a house, with every wound kept and one to three new ones, health 15 lower, nothing bandaged, half the carried things thrown around, and the driver dead or gone.
A journey can be fatal
When a crash or a collapse happens there is a chance that nobody survives it and the character really dies behind the black screen. Never on the first rescue of a character.
Trouble on the way (0 to 4)

How often something goes wrong while the character is being moved. 0 never, 1 calm, 2 normal, 3 harsh, 4 brutal. At normal about one journey in four has an incident and about one in twenty-five ends with a crash or a dead rescuer. Distance, night, rain, wounds, earlier rescues and who is carrying all move the odds, and each incident makes the next more likely.
Warning signs
Most incidents are announced by a line on the black screen just before they happen.
Malicious: the gambler
Flips a coin for everything. Each wound is either wrapped cleanly or left alone, and half of what was carried is kept.
Gifts earn goodwill
Makes the mod gentler. Food or medicine left beside a thank-you note (two things or more) makes up for one earlier bad visit with that person. Off: a gift is only a gift.
Strangers leave something
Some rescuers leave things next to the character: a little food and water, a snack, a clean bandage, a blade and a ration, tins and a crowbar, meat and fishing line.
Malicious: the grave robber

Takes the character for dead, strips everything including the clothes and dumps them nearby in the open. No bandages, no painkillers, no journal, every wound kept, health 10 lower, a shorter and lower recovery floor.
Hammering
The hammering part after arriving in the house. Needs the window boarding and the sounds to be on.
Malicious: the harvester
Takes blood. Clean dressings, but the character wakes weaker and for four days health cannot rise above 70 and stamina stays low.
Hazmat suit fools some zombies
While you wear a hazmat suit, 2 in 5 zombies without one do not notice you until you are within 2 squares. Once one has noticed you, it keeps after you. Hit one and it is no longer fooled.
The dead in hazmat suits cannot bite
A zombie still sealed in a hazmat suit cannot bite, scratch or cut you through it. Where it grabs you, it only hurts.
Hazmat zombies ignore hazmat suits
Zombies wearing hazmat suits leave you alone while you wear one too. Hit one and it comes for you like any other.
Health floor while recovering
Lowest overall health (0-100) during the recovery period. Keep it above the health that counts as dying. A crash, a rescuer who died and some malicious strangers lower it by a few points.
Health that counts as dying
The rescue starts when overall health (0-100) drops below this. Higher is safer, because a single hit that takes the character from above this number straight to zero cannot be caught.
Heard from afar: an alarm
Heard only until day 60 (or "Outbreak scenes stop after", if sooner), then never again.
Heard from afar: a car crash
Can be heard for the whole game. Needs "Heard scenes" on.
Heard from afar: fire engines
Heard only until day 30 (or "Outbreak scenes stop after", if sooner), then never again.
Heard from afar: a last stand
Can be heard for the whole game. Needs "Heard scenes" on.
Heard from afar: army vehicles
Heard only until day 45 (or "Outbreak scenes stop after", if sooner), then never again.
Heard from afar: a gunfight
Can be heard for the whole game. Needs "Heard scenes" on.
Heard from afar: sirens
Heard only until day 30 (or "Outbreak scenes stop after", if sooner), then never again.
The hoarder can find you
Does not empty the house, so the cupboards still hold their loot under a great deal of rubbish. Poor care: dirty rags and no painkillers.
Hours unconscious
Roughly how many game hours pass behind the black screen. With a fixed waking hour the real number is stretched or shortened by up to half a day to land in that window.
The hunter can find you
Takes the character to a camp in the open instead of a house. No walls and no boards. Leaves meat, a knife and line.
Indoors: lower rescue chance (percent)
Taken off the rescue chance when the character goes down under a roof, where nobody passing can see them. Outdoors the chance is unchanged.
Lost items stay where you fell
Lost items are dropped on the ground where it happened, so you can go back for them. Whatever a stranger takes as payment is gone either way. When off everything is gone.
Leave a journal
The journal counts them

The rescuer writes down how many zombies were dealt with where the character fell, and roughly how many more stood within 20 tiles in each direction. The remark depends on the number and on who is writing. Nothing is written when there were none.
The character wakes up with a journal written by whoever found them. The text is put together fresh each time from what actually happened, in that stranger's own way of writing.
Near a known place: higher rescue chance (percent)

Added to the rescue chance when the character goes down close to a church, a medical building, a police or fire station, an army post, a gun shop or a school, because people still go there. Inside one of these the indoor loss does not apply. The open street changes nothing.
Near a known place: the matching rescuer (percent)

How often the rescuer is the kind of person who belongs there: the believer by a church, the nurse by a medical building or fire station, the soldier by a police station or army post, the hunter by a gun shop, the kid by a school. Otherwise the usual roll.
Near a known place: how close (tiles)
How close to the building the character has to be. 0 switches the whole thing off.
The last rescue is announced
When no further rescue is possible the journal and the character both say so.
Scenes look lived in
Round every scene: rubbish, junk, the odd bin, chair, table or cold campfire, blood, sometimes a body, and a mess on the floors inside. Nothing useful is added.
Lock the doors, leave the key
The outside doors are locked and the house key is put in the character's pocket. Nothing is locked if no key can be made.
Lose what was on the back
The weapon or tool attached to the back is left behind. A worn backpack is kept.
Loose items lost (percent)
Share of the loose items in the main inventory that is left behind. Clothes, bags, keys, maps and favourites are never taken.
Also take from bags
The share of lost items is also taken from inside the backpack and any other bag the character carries. Keys, maps, books and favourites are never taken.
Lose what was in the hands
Whatever the character was holding is left behind.
Malicious strangers (percent)
Chance that a new face is one of the malicious kinds below. Each kind can be switched off on its own. 0 means none of them ever appear.
Maximum distance (tiles)
The house is at most this far away. If no house exists in that range the closest fit is used.
Maximum rescues
Hard limit per character. 0 means no hard limit, only the falling chance.
Wounds that stay
Only this many of the worst wounded body parts come back under bandages. The rest are gone when the character wakes. A crash, a grave robber and saving yourself keep every wound.
Nurse cuts out a bite (percent)

Only the nurse can turn a bite into a deep wound and remove the infection, and only this often. Every other rescuer leaves the character bitten and infected, even under clean bandages. The infection does not advance while unconscious.
Amount of rubbish (percent)
How much rubbish is scattered around the character, through the house and in the yard. 100 is about sixty items, 0 is none.
Minimum distance (tiles)
The house the character wakes up in is at least this far from where they fell. Further takes longer behind the black screen.
They remember you

Every rescuer keeps a mood. Being found by the same person again within a few days wears it down: first less care, then a price, then they leave for good. Weeks without needing them repair it. Being rescued often makes new faces wary too. The thief is the exception and grows fond.
Nightmares (days)
For this many days after a rescue the character sometimes wakes from sleep in a panic. 0 turns it off.
No rescue when infected
Makes the mod harsher. Nobody saves a character carrying the infection: going down infected is a real death.
Hours too weak to run (at most)

After waking the character can only walk. This is the longest it can last: a character who wakes with no wounds gets a quarter of it, each wound adds to it, and a crash gives all of it. 0 switches it off.
Hours too weak to sprint (at most)
After waking the character cannot sprint. Scaled by how badly hurt they wake in the same way as running: a quarter of this with no wounds, all of it after a crash. 0 switches it off.
How often notes turn up (percent)
Scales every chance of finding a note. 100 is the default, 0 means no notes at all, 300 is three times as many.
Notes in houses
Notes can be found in drawers, cupboards, desks and on floors when a house is first searched. At the default frequency about one house in five has one, and the first two come twice as easily.
Notes on the street
Now and then a note lies outside, on a road or a pavement.
Notes on zombies
Killed zombies can carry a note. Their clothes decide what kind: soldiers carry military notes, medics medical notes, hazmat suits CDC reports.
Outbreak scenes stop after (days)

After this many days the collapse is over: no new roadblocks, checkpoints, evacuations or sirens happen. What they left is still found, gone quiet, but only in places you have not been since. Burning houses, loudspeakers, fresh crashes and shop alarms stop for good. Survivors' scenes go on. A world that starts months after the apocalypse counts those months too.
Outposts: most days before one appears
And at most this many. The countdown starts over somewhere else if you walk into the place before it ends.
Outposts: fewest days before one appears
Once a place is picked, the outpost appears there after at least this many days.
Outposts: days away before ground counts as new
Outposts only appear on ground you have not been to. Ground you left this many days ago counts as new again.
Outposts

Fenced outposts the army, the police, the doctors or other survivors set up to hold a town, long since overrun. At most four to a town, one of each kind. A place is picked on ground you have never been to, and the outpost appears there after a few days. Walk into that place before then and it is picked somewhere else.
Painkillers in the pocket
The character wakes with a box of painkillers in their inventory.
The pair can find you
Two people who disagree. One cleans the wounds, the other takes the weapon and half of what was carried, and both write in the journal.
Other places than a house
Sometimes the character wakes in a church, a school, a shed or a very small house instead. If none exists within range a normal house is used.
The prepper can find you
Boards the doors as well as the windows, from the inside, and takes the weapon in hand. Leaves water, tins, antibiotics and the crowbar needed to get out.
Difficulty (0 follows the game mode, 1 gentle, 2 harsh, 3 fast, 4 standard)

0 reads the game mode and matches it: Apocalypse is standard, Rising is gentle, Extinction is harsh, Outbreak is fast. A sandbox world is judged by its zombies, loot and injuries. Any option you change yourself always wins over the difficulty. Gentle: a certain first rescue, less trouble on the way, few malicious strangers, no fatal journeys, a kinder nurse, more health on waking, less lost. Harsh: the first rescue is a 30 percent chance, more trouble, more malice, a harder nurse, less health, more lost, rescues run out sooner. Fast: a certain first rescue, shorter knockouts, black screen and recovery. Standard: the options as they are, a 60 percent first rescue.
Malicious: the quack
Confident and wrong. The painkillers and antibiotics left in the pocket are vitamins with new labels, one wound is infected, and the character wakes drowsy and nauseous.
Days before a used area turns up something new
An area you keep spending time in goes quiet. Nothing new is placed there until you have stayed away this many days. Nothing ever appears in front of you.
Silence the world
All game sound is muted while the character is being moved, so nothing real is heard. It comes back for the staged sounds once they have arrived. The ambience stays muted until the character wakes.
Recovery period (hours)
For this many game hours after waking, wounds, hunger and thirst cannot bring health below the floor. A zombie within three tiles switches this protection off.
Size of an area (tiles)
The map is divided into areas of this size. Each area has its own people: survivors, police, soldiers, medics and more, each with their own health and mood.
Rescue chance (percent)

Chance that the first near-death ends in a rescue instead of a death. Left at 60 it follows the game mode: certain in Rising and Outbreak, 60 in Apocalypse, 30 in Extinction. Set 100 for a certain first rescue everywhere.
Notes from your rescuers
The strangers from your own save, the warden, the nurse, the arsonist and the rest, leave notes in the world too. Rare: about one per area each.
Discover the map along the way

When off, the map only shows where it happened and where the character woke up, not the line in between. Parts of the route you had already explored stay explored. When on, the whole route is uncovered on the map.
The scavenger can find you

A rescuer who takes everything: every item, every bag and all the clothes the character is wearing. In return every wound gets a clean bandage and a medical kit is left in the inventory. When off, this one never appears.
The shop with its alarm still set
Happens only in days 0 to 25 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). It is only ever something happening right now, so nothing of it is left to find later.
Ambulances that never arrived

Happens in days 0 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Hiding in the attic
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 2 on, for the whole game.
Roadblocks

Happens in days 0 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Breached quarantine

A house the health department sealed with the sick inside, and it did not hold: the front door broken out, sandbags and a triage on the lawn, body bags, a FEMA van and a patrol car, the street closed off and the hazmat crew still walking. Only at a house whose front door faces a street. Days 3 to 30, most in the second and third week.
Basement bunkers
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 14 on, for the whole game.
Campsites
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 10 on, for the whole game.
Checkpoints

Happens in days 0 to 45 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Triage outside the clinic

Happens in days 0 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Survivor compounds
Survivors' doing: it can turn up for the whole game.
Army convoys

Happens in days 0 to 40 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Delivery trucks

Happens in days 0 to 40 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Families who almost made it to the car

Happens in days 0 to 20 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Evacuation points

Happens in days 0 to 14 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Burning houses
The fire department scene sets the house it is at on fire, far from anywhere you have been lately and never near a Home Sense home. The fire is real and can spread like any fire.
How often scenes turn up (percent)
Scales the chance of every scene. 100 is the default.
Fuel runs gone wrong
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 7 on, for the whole game.
The gun shop siege

Happens in days 1 to 60 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Highway jams

A very long traffic jam out on a highway: everyone tried to leave the same way, the cars nose to tail with their doors open, luggage and boxes along the verges. Only on a long straight road with no building within 30 squares. Most of them in the first week; from day 31 the cars are burnt out, in new jams and in the ones already there.
Holdouts

Happens in days 3 to 90 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
A car through a house wall

Happens in days 0 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Burning houses and the fire department
Happens only in days 0 to 20 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). It is only ever something happening right now, so nothing of it is left to find later.
Last stands in houses
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 1 on, for the whole game.
Leftovers of old scenes

Once an outbreak scene's days are over, what it left (a roadblock, a checkpoint, a jam of cars) can still be found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. Off: outbreak scenes simply stop after their days.
Loudspeaker vans
Happens only in days 0 to 12 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). It is only ever something happening right now, so nothing of it is left to find later.
Mass graves

Happens in days 5 to 60 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.

Scene sounds draw zombies

Like the game's own distant gunfire: you hear a scene's shots, crashes and sirens from the way they came, and they make real noise where they happen, so the dead around there go to it. Sirens and alarms you set off up close draw them too. When off they are only sound.
Scene overseer

Keeps the world believable as a whole: the same scene rarely repeats nearby or back to back, areas that already have scenes get fewer new ones, scenes of one story (army, police, medical, panic, survivors) gather a little, the stages of the outbreak favour their own stories, and two scenes never share the same ground. Also keeps a count of every scene for the log. Off: scenes are picked as before.
Patrol cars

A patrol car stopped on the road with its lights still going and the doors open, the officer down or walking, the one they stopped a little way ahead. Every second siren you hear leaves one in the direction it went; a few appear on their own. Days 1 to 21.
The police station's last stand

Happens in days 0 to 21 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Prison transports

Happens in days 0 to 21 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Protest grounds

A protest on a shopping street that turned into looting, fires and a police line, from day 2 to day 7. Only on a long straight street with a cluster of shops around it (at least 4 shops within 30 squares, making up at least 4 in 10 of the buildings there), never in a neighbourhood of houses. The shop fronts along it get spray paint and smashed windows.
Quarantined houses

Happens in days 2 to 40 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Quiet rooms
Survivors' doing: it can turn up from day 3 on, for the whole game.
Reused army posts

An army checkpoint survivors moved into, on a straight road with no house within 15 squares (no town needed). Happens in days 3 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Shelters in schools and churches

Happens in days 3 to 60 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
A car through a shop front

Happens in days 0 to 30 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Survivor tolls

Survivors holding the road into a town: a fenced camp with a gate across the road, fires and lamps kept going, a notice for whoever comes by. Nobody is there when you arrive. Only on a straight road at the edge of a town (no house within 20 squares, a town within 120), never near the army's checkpoints, from day 8 on.
Traffic jams

Happens in days 0 to 14 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). "Its days, then what is left": after that, what it left is still found, gone quiet, in places you have not been since. "Only in its own days": after that, never.
Fresh car wrecks
Happens only in days 0 to 10 (never after "Outbreak scenes stop after"). It is only ever something happening right now, so nothing of it is left to find later.
Scenes
Places where something happened: crashes, blockades, checkpoints, camps, bunkers and more. They are placed in areas you are not in.
Text on the black screen
Short lines appear on the black screen describing what the character half notices while they are out.
Offer the choice to save yourself
Seconds to choose
With no answer in this time the character lets go.

When the character goes down, a bar shows the odds of pulling through alone, built from first aid skill, clean bandages, disinfectant, traits, wounds, zombies nearby, shelter, weather and hunger. Choose to try alone, which uses up your own supplies and kills the character if it fails, or to let go and take the usual chance that someone finds you. A bite caps the bar very low.
You can be shot at
Someone you never see fires at you. Out in the open the shots are more likely to hit, near houses they mostly miss.
Shots can hit
When off, every shot at you misses.
Things already gone at the site (percent)
Chance for each item left where the character fell to have been taken by someone else before it can be fetched.
Note where you fell
The stranger leaves a scrap of paper on the ground where it happened, for the day you come back for your things.
Enter skips ahead on the black screen
Press Enter to move past the lines while dying, on the journey and the hammering. What happens and the hours that pass stay the same; the journal still tells all of it.
The sniper
Rarely, a shooter follows you for a day, missing a few times. Later you can find where they watched you from.
The soldier can find you
Confiscates firearms and ammunition, leaves a blade, a ration and water, clean dressings and a splint, four planks on every window.
Scenes you hear first
Gunfire, a crash, screaming or a generator from a direction, and something to find there later.
Sounds behind the black screen

Plays the game's own sounds to go with the lines on the black screen: a body being dragged, effort, a car door, an engine, a gate, a door, hammering, cloth ripping, bandaging, drawers, eating, a key ring, a lock.
Notes that lead somewhere (percent)
Share of notes that point to something real. The item is placed in a container nearby first and the note only hints at where. No map marker.
Tiles per step
The character is moved to the house in steps of this many tiles behind the black screen, because the game refuses one long move. Lower it if the character does not arrive.
Different rescuers

The person who finds the character is an ordinary survivor or one of the special kinds, each treating wounds, taking things, leaving things and writing differently, and the same one can find you again. When off it is always a nameless drifter and the options on the People page do nothing.
Share of survivors (percent)
How many of the new faces are ordinary survivors. The rest are the special kinds.
Ordinary survivors

The most common rescuer is an ordinary survivor: a person with a name, a former job, a temper and a reason for helping, made up for this save. What they do is always the plain rescue. Who they are and how they write is different for each one.
The thief takes something you wear
The thief keeps one piece of clothing or jewellery, such as shoes, a jacket, a hat or a watch.
Character talks
The character says a few lines after waking and when returning to the place it happened.
Seconds each line stays on the black screen
How long one line of text is shown before the next. The journey lasts as long as its lines need, so a higher number also means a longer black screen.
Thank-you notes

For three days after waking you can leave a note where you woke for the one who saved you (needs a pen or pencil and paper). Whatever lies next to it goes with it. The next time they find you, they answer. Nobody who meant you harm is thanked.
Trader visit chance per sleep (percent)
Chance that a trader comes by while you sleep, once the days below have passed.
Days between trader visits
At least this many days pass between two trader notes at your door.
Traders
While you sleep, a trader may leave a note at the door. Leave something where they ask, and maybe something comes back while you are away.
Journey sounds (seconds, at least)

After the character has arrived, the journey is played back as lines and sounds: being dragged, the car, the gate. It lasts at least this long, and longer when its lines need more time at the chosen seconds per line. 0 skips it.
Wake at a fixed hour
The character always wakes inside the window below, by sleeping a little longer or shorter than the hours unconscious.
Wake no earlier than (hour)
Start of the waking window, 0 to 23. Default 3 in the morning.
Health on waking
Overall health (0-100) the character wakes up with.
Hunger on waking (percent)
68 is just below the point where starving starts to cost health.
Thirst on waking (percent)
68 is just below the point where thirst starts to cost health.
Wake no later than (hour)
End of the waking window, 0 to 23. Default 5 in the morning.
Malicious: the warden

Boards the door from the outside, locks it and keeps the key. Little food and water. A tool to break out is hidden somewhere in the house. If the character is still inside when the warden returns a day or two later, everything carried is taken again.
Chapter II: Out There

Chapter II, added in 3.0: the places, sounds and notes you find out in the world, traders, scenes and events. Off by default. When off, the mod is the rescue only, exactly as in 2.0. Turn it on here for a new game; in a save that does not have it, you are asked once when you start playing, and can change it later by right-clicking the ground. The containment soldier has its own switch.
